_comment: VOICE CONVERSION, not synthesis. Feed in a real recorded performance and come out the other side in a different voice, keeping the original timing, breaths, emphasis and mistakes. For a presenter ad this usually beats TTS outright: you are converting an actual human performance rather than asking a model to invent one, so everything that makes a read sound human is preserved by construction.
_why_here: RVC has NO standalone ComfyUI node. The registry's `ComfyUI-RVC` entry is an unclaimed stub with zero published versions, so `comfy-node-install ComfyUI-RVC` resolves and installs nothing - a silent no-op rather than an error. tts_audio_suite is the only maintained route, which is why this workflow lives in the bench image rather than a production one.
_licence: RVC itself is MIT (RVC-Project/Retrieval-based-Voice-Conversion-WebUI, still the canonical repo). The risk here is NOT the licence - it is voice-likeness rights in the target model. A community .pth trained on a celebrity or a YouTuber is a legal problem regardless of how permissive the code is. Use only models trained on voices we have written consent for. Applio is the best-maintained fork but has announced wind-down.
_models: RVC target models are 100-300MB .pth files plus an optional .index for retrieval. Language-agnostic - it converts timbre, not text - so one model serves both the EN and FR reads, which is exactly what a bilingual campaign wants and what no TTS lane gives you for free.
_schema_drift: Input names read from tts_audio_suite v5.8.10 and will drift. If validation 400s, GET /object_info on a running instance and re-read rather than guessing.
